The patient was transferred to the CCU on February 6th for torsades de pointes. She received magnesium and was started on standing magnesium repletion. Disopyramide was discontinued due to long QT syndrome. She experienced a second episode of ventricular tachycardia with loss of consciousness, requiring external shocks, intubation, and administration of epinephrine, atropine, and lidocaine. She was started on isoproterenol and levophed for hypotension. A femoral line was placed. After the episode, she had occasional non-sustained ventricular tachycardia but no further sustained VT. On February 8th, she was weaned off levophed and the groin line was removed. Around noon, she developed supraventricular tachycardia with heart rates in the 160s, trending down to 120s, which appeared to be atrial fibrillation. Isoproterenol was discontinued, and she was started on metoprolol, which was uptitrated to diltiazem with improved heart rate control. She was subsequently extubated. She had residual chest wall pain after CPR and rib films revealed non displaced rib fractures. She initially had left-sided failure with pulmonary edema and pleural effusions, likely secondary to atrial fibrillation. Severe mitral regurgitation was found on TTE. Cardiac surgery was consulted and felt a mitral valve replacement and tricuspid valve repair were required. The patient underwent a cardiac catheterization which showed clean coronaries. She was restarted on losartan before discharge.
